attempts.narrative: T1 I went straight at the Weakness Policy, which the dossier itself lists as the crack: Weavile's Knock Off into Metang is 2x (Dark into Psychic), carries the +50 percent item-removal bonus, and takes the Policy off the board in the same action. It also killed a level 38 Metang outright from full, which I did not expect. Duskull spent that turn on Protect rather than on the authored Shadow Sneak activation, so the combo never fired on the only turn it could have. Metang used Bullet Punch into Weavile for 78 before it died. T2 Weavile's Knock Off one-shot Hattrem the same way and removed its Eviolite; Incineroar's Knock Off took Duskull to 20 and removed its Eviolite; Duskull burned Weavile with Will-O-Wisp. T3 Butterfree came in and used Rage Powder, which correctly pulled my Flare Blitz away from the 20 HP Duskull - but Flare Blitz is 2x into Bug/Flying and killed Butterfree through its Focus Sash anyway, because Triple Axel had already landed two hits on it. Weavile died to Life Orb recoil plus burn. T4 Rillaboom came in and Grassy Glide finished Duskull.

strategy_checks.check: Duskull activates Metang's Weakness Policy with Shadow Sneak
strategy_checks.result: FAIL - the authored tactic never fired
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 was the only turn the combo was ever available: both leads were at full HP, Metang was holding an unspent Weakness Policy, and Shadow Sneak is priority so it resolves before anything I could do except another priority move. Duskull chose Protect. Metang chose Bullet Punch. By the time Duskull did select Shadow Sneak, on turn 3, Metang had been dead for two turns and the move went into my Weavile as an ordinary priority attack, which was then correct. This is the team's entire identity - the dossier's tactic line, its ALLY_COMBO strategy flag and its 'Could it be cooler?' note are all about this one interaction - and it did not happen. See ai_defects.

strategy_checks.check: Activation is not repeated after consumption and not aimed at a blocked recipient
strategy_checks.evidence: There was no repetition to criticise because there was no activation. The one Shadow Sneak that was used, on T3, went into a live enemy rather than a dead ally, so the guard against a pointless friendly hit is at least working in the negative direction.

strategy_checks.check: Metang converts the Weakness Policy boost
strategy_checks.evidence: Metang never received a boost and was KO'd on turn 1 by a single Knock Off. Its one action, Bullet Punch into Weavile, was super effective (Steel into Ice) for 78 of Weavile's 107, which is the correct target and move for an unboosted Metang facing a faster Ice/Dark.

strategy_checks.check: Butterfree supplies Sleep Powder and Rage Powder redirection
strategy_checks.result: PARTIAL - Rage Powder PASS, Sleep Powder NOT OBSERVED
strategy_checks.evidence: Butterfree had exactly one turn and used Rage Powder, which successfully pulled Incineroar's Flare Blitz off a 20 HP Duskull. That is a correct, well-timed redirection: it saved Duskull for a turn. It did not save Butterfree, because Flare Blitz is 2x into Bug/Flying and Triple Axel had already broken the Focus Sash in the same turn. Compound Eyes Sleep Powder never got a board.

strategy_checks.check: Hattrem supplies Magic Bounce and Life Dew
strategy_checks.evidence: Hattrem was KO'd from full by one Knock Off on the turn it came in, before selecting an action.

strategy_checks.result: PASS on paper, and it is the member that actually performed
strategy_checks.evidence: Duskull was the last one standing and the only member that got more than one useful turn out of the fight: Protect, Will-O-Wisp (which burned Weavile and, with Life Orb, is what actually killed it), then Shadow Sneak. 98 HP with 252/252 Careful and an Eviolite is genuinely awkward to remove - my Incineroar Knock Off only took it to 20 at 2x.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL BUT IT COST THE TEAM ITS PLAN: the Protect blocked Incineroar's Flare Blitz, which had been retargeted onto Duskull after Metang fainted, so it denied real damage and saved Incineroar's recoil too. The problem is what it replaced. Turn 1 was the single turn on which the authored Weakness Policy activation was possible, and Duskull spent it guarding. Graded as a guard: fine. Graded against the plan: this is the whole fight.

protect_ledger_note: One opposing Protect in four turns. Not empty and not repeated. Butterfree and Hattrem both carry Protect and neither had the chance to use it.

ai_defects.defect: Authored ally-combo tactic did not fire on the only turn it was available
ai_defects.board: Opponent Duskull (98/98, Eviolite, Levitate, holds Shadow Sneak) and Metang (129/129, Clear Body, holding an unspent WEAKNESS_POLICY) against my Incineroar (148/148) and Weavile (107/107). The team carries strategy ALLY_COMBO,REDIRECTION and the bespoke tactic line 'ACTIVATE DUSKULL SHADOW_SNEAK METANG'.
ai_defects.chosen: Duskull used Protect; Metang used Bullet Punch.
ai_defects.better_action: Duskull uses Shadow Sneak on its own Metang. Shadow Sneak is priority +1 so it resolves before every non-priority action on the board, Ghost is super effective into Metang's Psychic half so it satisfies the Weakness Policy condition, and Duskull is built with a zero Attack IV, Careful nature and no Attack investment precisely so the friendly hit is small. That single action gives Metang +2 Attack and +2 Special Attack before it moves. Metang then attacks at +2 instead of throwing an unboosted Bullet Punch.
ai_defects.note: I cannot tell from the driver whether the tactic was evaluated and scored below Protect, or whether it was never a candidate. Either way the observable behaviour is that the team's authored identity did not execute on a board that was ideal for it. This is the one finding in my block that I would ask the AI side to trace, because the same ALLY_COMBO/ACTIVATE machinery is shared with other authored activation teams (Shayla's ACTIVATE SIMIPOUR SURF MARACTUS in this same block did fire - see play_order 92 - so the mechanism is not globally dead, and the difference between a spread Surf onto a Storm Drain ally and a targeted friendly Shadow Sneak is the thing worth looking at).

ai_notes: Apart from the T1 tactic failure there was no bad choice. Bullet Punch into a faster Ice/Dark, Will-O-Wisp onto the Life Orb attacker (which is what actually killed Weavile), Rage Powder to pull damage off a 20 HP partner, and Shadow Sneak once the ally target was gone - all correct.

Will-O-Wisp target selection deserves credit: Duskull picked the Life Orb Weavile over the Incineroar, and Incineroar is a Fire type that cannot be burned at all. It did not waste the move on an immune target.

The fight exposes a build fragility rather than a level problem: two level-38 members were each removed by a single Knock Off from a level-36 Life Orb Weavile, because Dark is 2x into both and Knock Off gets its +50 percent while removing their items. Metang at 252 HP / 252 Attack and Hattrem at 252 HP / 240 SpDef both have essentially no physical Defense investment.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: first-attempt win with one player faint. Butterfree is the lowest member by a wide margin (35 against 38/38/38) and is not the ace. +1 only. I want to be explicit that I do not think levels are this encounter's problem - three members are already at cap+2 and the fight was still one-sided because the authored combo did not fire and because Knock Off answers three quarters of the roster. The AI defect above is the real fix; this +1 is the rule being applied, not my diagnosis.

could_this_be_cooler: The concept is already cool and the dossier's reasoning for it is sound - a deliberately weak-hitting Duskull whose job is to punch its own partner is a genuinely memorable idea for a Trick House room, and it is distinct from Aisha's critical-hit engine. But the execution has two problems that are worth fixing together. First, the whole team dies to one move: Knock Off is 2x into Duskull, Metang and Hattrem, and it removes the Eviolite/Weakness Policy that three of the four are built around, so a single well-chosen Dark attacker unpicks the entire concept in two turns. Second, the combo is all-or-nothing on turn 1. I would keep Duskull and Metang exactly as they are and change Hattrem, whose Magic Bounce and Life Dew contributed nothing and whose Psychic typing is a third Knock Off target: a Steel or Dark partner there, or simply an Assault Vest instead of the third Eviolite, would mean that losing the activation turn does not lose the fight. The Butterfree is the right kind of second layer and should stay.
